big-news.text: The British carrier HMS *Prince of Wales* (284 m, about 700 crew) sails into the Oslofjord today for the Atlantic Future Forum, escorted by British and Norwegian ships.
Norges Bank kept the policy rate at 4.5% yesterday. Inflation is still too high, and they say they may hike again if needed. The next decision is Dec 17.
A 29-year-old got nine years for three attempted murders in the Tveita centre shooting from July 2025. Two people were hit and survived.

whats-changing.text: A proposal to raise the national e-scooter age limit from 12 to 16 is out for hearing, with a deadline of Feb 5, 2027, and an aim for spring 2027.
Oslo is cutting rental e-scooters from 16,000 to a max of 12,000, shifting 4,000 slots to e-bikes, and setting a 16 age floor, likely from April 1.

oslo.text: Parts of Festningskaia at Akershus are closed for the carrier visit, with more military presence around the harbour.
Blasting in Prinsdal went wrong on Thursday. Rocks hit a house, nobody was hurt, and the police are investigating.

be-aware.text: Fog plus near-freezing temps this weekend in southern Norway means black-ice risk. Winter shoes help, and winter tires if you're driving.
No drones within about 3.7 km of the military ships, and boats must keep about 1 nautical mile from the carrier.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: Fjord Oslo's free light-art trail along the waterfront (Tjuvholmen to Akershusstranda) runs tonight through Sunday, 18:00 to 23:00. Saturday evening is an easy first night back.
Oslo Zine Fest has a free market at ROM (Maridalsveien 3) from 12:00 to 17:00 on Saturday and Sunday.
The Frank Znort Quartet plays a free show at BLÅ on Sunday at 15:00.
